overview.title: Welcome to Asilah — Atlantic breeze, whitewashed walls, and street art
overview.p1: Perched on northern Morocco's Atlantic coast, Asilah is a peaceful enclave known for its pristine whitewashed medina, vibrant murals painted by international artists, and dramatic sea-facing Portuguese ramparts.
overview.p2: Whether you visit for the annual Cultural Moussem, wander quiet blue-accented alleyways, enjoy freshly caught grilled fish by the harbour, or head south to the golden expanse of Paradise Beach, Asilah offers an effortless coastal retreat.

places.title: Must-visit places in Asilah
places.subtitle: Artistic alleyways, historic bastions, and wide ocean beaches.

art_medina.title: The Art Medina
art_medina.desc: Whitewashed alleyways adorned with outdoor murals and wrought-iron balconies.

ramparts_krikia.title: Ramparts & Borj Krikia
ramparts_krikia.desc: 15th-century sea fortifications with the city's iconic Atlantic sunset lookout.

paradise_beach.title: Paradise Beach (Rmilat)
paradise_beach.desc: A vast, golden stretch of sand backed by cliffs, located 30 minutes south of town.

raissouni_palace.title: Raissouni Palace
raissouni_palace.desc: Early 20th-century Moorish palace built by a famed local leader, hosting art cultural workshops.

borj_kamra.title: Borj Al-Kamra Tower
borj_kamra.desc: A square Portuguese keep standing tall near the medina's main entrance gate.

corniche_harbour.title: Corniche & Port
corniche_harbour.desc: Lively evening promenade lined with seafood restaurants and views of blue fishing boats.

stays.title: Where to stay in Asilah? Our Favorites
stays.subtitle: From oceanfront boutique riads to whitewashed houses and relaxed beachfront stays, here are our top choices.

card1.name: Hotel Maison Garcia
card1.desc: A famous family-run hotel opposite the ramparts, known for its iconic Spanish-style seafood restaurant.

card2.name: Dar Oasis Medina
card2.desc: Charming whitewashed guesthouse tucked inside the art medina, featuring a roof terrace with ocean breeze.

card3.name: Hotel Zelis
card3.desc: Comfortable modern hotel located near the city center and main avenue, with swimming pool and breakfast.

card4.name: Asilah Marina Golf Resort
card4.desc: Self-catering apartments in a secure beachside complex with pools and garden areas, ideal for families.

booking_banner.title: Explore all stays in Asilah
booking_banner.desc: Compare real-time rates, read verified guest reviews, and enjoy free cancellation on most hotels and medina houses.

eat.title: Where to eat in Asilah
eat.subtitle: Fresh fried seafood, Spanish-influenced dining, and tea spots.

pepe.title: Casa Pepe
pepe.desc: Famous spot for fresh grilled fish, paella, and Spanish-Moroccan dishes.

port.title: Portside Fried Fish Stalls
port.desc: Simple outdoor tables serving the catch of the day with tomato salad and harissa.

ramparts.title: Ramparts Tea Terrace
ramparts.desc: Mint tea, fresh juice, and Moroccan pastries with panoramic ocean views.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: The medina is entirely pedestrian. Petits taxis or horse carriages are easy to hire for trips to Paradise Beach.

bargain.title: Art & Moussem
bargain.desc: The annual Arts Festival takes place in July/August, bringing fresh murals and cultural concerts.

water.title: Atmosphere
water.desc: Asilah is very quiet compared to Tangier. Perfect for relaxing, photography, and ocean sunsets.

daytrips.title: Best day trips from Asilah
daytrips.subtitle: Explore northern Morocco's Atlantic coast and nearby cultural hubs.

tangier.title: Tangier (45 min)
tangier.desc: Discover the Kasbah, Cap Spartel, Hercules Caves, and vibrant cafes.

larache.title: Larache & Lixus (35 min)
larache.desc: Explore ancient Phoenician-Roman ruins at Lixus and Larache's Spanish square.

chefchaouen.title: Chefchaouen (2 hrs)
chefchaouen.desc: A scenic drive into the Rif mountains to visit Morocco's famous Blue Pearl.

q1.question: How many days should I stay in Asilah?
q1.answer: One or two days are perfect for exploring the medina, enjoying seafood, watching Atlantic sunsets, and spending an afternoon at Paradise Beach.

q2.question: When is the Asilah Arts Festival held?
q2.answer: The International Cultural Moussem of Asilah is held annually in mid-summer (usually July or August), attracting international artists who repaint the medina wall murals.

q3.question: How do I get from Tangier to Asilah?
q3.answer: Asilah is 45 km south of Tangier. You can take a direct ONCF train (30 mins), a grand taxi, or drive via the A1 highway.

q4.question: Is Asilah good for beach lovers?
q4.answer: Yes, Asilah has long sandy beaches extending both north and south, with Paradise Beach (Rmilat) being one of the most stunning coastal spots in northern Morocco.

itinerary.title: Suggested 2-day plan for Asilah
itinerary.subtitle: Art exploration, rampart sunsets, and ocean relaxation.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Enter via Bab Al-Kasbah, photograph painted murals, and explore quiet whitewashed streets.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Visit Raissouni Palace (if open during events) and pass by Borj Al-Kamra tower.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Gather at Borj Krikia on the ramparts for sunset over the Atlantic, followed by seafood near the port.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Take a taxi or horse carriage south to Paradise Beach (Rmilat) for a relaxing coastal morning.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Enjoy tea in seasonal beach shacks or walk along the cliff-backed golden sands.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Return to town for a final evening stroll along the lively beachside corniche.
